I’ve built the model around your stated goal: **Weekly support capacity of at least 100 tickets per week**, with no deadline.

It uses your figures:
- Existing team capacity: **80 tickets per week**
- One additional specialist: **about 20 tickets per week**, with a stated range of **10–30**
- Capacity is defined as existing capacity plus additional specialist capacity.
- **Keep current staffing** holds today’s staffing.
- **Add one specialist** adds one specialist.

Olumi also drafted a **part-time specialist** alternative and two possible risks, but these are explicitly Olumi’s additions, not yours, and are excluded from the first pass unless you choose to include them.

A provisional first pass has run automatically on this newly drafted model. It is not validated and does not put an option forward. The key assumption to challenge is whether the specialist’s **10–30 tickets per week** contribution is realised immediately, or reduced during onboarding or ramp-up.

‘Role fit limits ticket resolution’: ‘Add one specialist’ relies on this not happening. This model can't yet apply that risk to that option alone, so the Run leaves it out, and that option's chance doesn't include it yet.

‘Part-time coverage gaps’: ‘Add part-time specialist’ relies on this not happening. This model can't yet apply that risk to that option alone, so the Run leaves it out.

‘Add part-time specialist’ is Olumi’s suggestion, so it was left out of this comparison until you add it.

Olumi added 2 risks for you to consider. They're Olumi's suggestions, not yours; remove any that don't fit.

It rests most on how strongly ‘Additional specialists’ affects ‘Additional specialist capacity’, at the size you set: if that effect is weaker than that, the chance falls.
